original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: One new complete call type DUO_{j,k}: z += B_j x_j + B_k x_k (two-source combined toggle, sources read-only) added to the frozen universal-connector alphabet; exact Pareto frontier of (source calls k, toggle-adds W) for full 32-mask coverage on the three-source tiny instance and the frozen five-source all-31-row batch.
scope_change_reason: The card asked for one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample without naming the operation; the operation is fixed to the two-source combined toggle and the domains to n=3 (falsification-first) then n=5 (the frozen 74-query instance), with n=4 recorded as a side row. Same card, same connector object and boundary.
bottleneck_link: Connector call cost enters the recursive interface through complete-call pricing; the DUO extension cuts root queries 74 -> 72 at identical toggle-adds (saving exactly 2 per-call overheads o). Side result relative to the paid recursive profile: no physical supplier instance of this connector interface exists, the predecessor limitation, unchanged here.
stop_rule: Require a witness with (k, W) <= (10, 12) or a complete exclusion of that domain; one bounded pivot to weight-3 steps maximum; stop after the s <= 10 census regardless.
evidence: Scoped finite result: unique Pareto profile (10 calls, 12 toggle-adds) for the five-source DUO alphabet, (5, 6) for n=3, (6, 8) for the n=4 side row; k=9 excluded by a complete zero-cover census of all 9-point sets; batch 72 queries at 74 adds vs frozen 74 at 74. No new kappa; no supplier instance. Command: python3 -B research/duo-toggle-connector/verify.py -> PASS_DUO_TOGGLE_CONNECTOR queries=72->74 adds=74 pareto=(10,12); independent s9 scan 7,888,725 sets / 0 full covers; 945 control histogram matches research/universal-connector-boundary; 12 dense dirty replays at L=1,2,3; 4 mutation controls detected; CERTIFICATE.json with sorted-record SHA256 and witness words.

open_questions.question: Does a real supplier boundary admit the DUO call at positive per-call overhead o?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The entire saving is 2o; with no per-call overhead the extension gains nothing.
open_questions.first_step: Instantiate the predecessor dense-bit-matrix leaf for one DUO call and price its entry/exit frame against two singleton calls.
open_questions.blocked_by: No physical instance of the connector interface exists in the selected supplier.

open_questions.question: What is the exact Pareto profile of the DUO alphabet at n=6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1185 fixes f(6)=16 in the singleton alphabet; C(12,2)=66 >= 63 allows s=12 difference covers in principle.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate s=11 and s=12 difference covers of F2^6 with the collision prune and search wt<=2 walkability.
open_questions.blocked_by: C(63,11) enumeration needs the prune to bite before the search is cheap.

open_questions.question: Can a charged weight-3 step lower W below 12 at k=10?
open_questions.why_it_matters: W=12 equals the frozen add count; lowering it would save adds as well as calls.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat this census with steps of weight <= 3 and a charged three-source call.
